howToUse.coreLevel: Every case runs through the statistics core on the counts given in data (both runners unless runners says otherwise). A plan case first normalises its plan (or derives it from legacy, section 9; a multiclass derivation takes k, the number of labels that occur in the target column, from data) and must reproduce expected.normalizedPlan exactly and expected.planSha256, the SHA-256 of its RFC 8785 canonical JSON.
howToUse.comparison: Numbers: |actual - expected| <= tolerance (p-values: absolute + relative). Members and descriptive entries are matched by memberId, groups by group; reasons are compared as sets; all other fields exactly. The expected_calibration_error and r2 intervals are null at core level because the engine adds them by bootstrap end to end.
howToUse.outputMapping: Section 11 of the specification maps every fixture field to the emitted result: headline, members and descriptive entries become metrics, groups become the headline's slices, decision becomes result.decision.
howToUse.rowExpansion: For endToEnd cases, expand each group in order into rows (label, prediction, group): tp -> (1,1), fp -> (0,1), fn -> (1,0), tn -> (0,0); selection-only groups: selected -> (1,1), others -> (0,0). The binary labels are declared: positive '1', negative '0'; a runner must evaluate data in which only one of them occurs (GC-15, GC-37). Multiclass: matrix[i][j] rows with label labels[i] and prediction labels[j]. Regression: target = targets[i] (0 when absent) and prediction = target + errors[i]. Calibration bins: label 1 for positives, score = meanScore, prediction 1 when score >= 0.5. A legacy case runs with its legacy configuration: a hosted_config case directly in the hosted runner and through the worker translation in the engine; an engine_thresholds case directly in the engine.

cases.title: Three-class confusion matrix: accuracy, macro recall (balanced accuracy) and macro F1; macro precision descriptive
Regression errors: MAE and RMSE with normal-approximation intervals; R2 descriptive
Fisher's exact test reference values (two-sided; tables with probability <= the observed one)
Everyone selected in both groups: Koopman replaces the zero-width Katz interval; the parity pass does not survive Bonferroni (only one label is observed)
Legacy hosted profile without a plan: derived criteria, minimums raised to the floors, the balanced-accuracy baseline, and descriptive precision, specificity and F1
Engine thresholds.values to a plan: the balanced-accuracy baseline, a Brier member, ECE descriptive, group bands and the configured minimums recorded
Three groups, all pairs: a 0.10 parity band at 30% selection with 500, 500 and 250 per group
Multi-member performance criterion in a family of three: one-sided lower and upper bands, balanced accuracy and F1
Equalized odds with per-group prevalence: a true TPR gap on the band edge makes the target unreachable
Multiclass criterion: accuracy and macro recall are computed, macro F1 is not, so the criterion is not_computed
Regression criterion: MAE and RMSE maxima under normal errors with standard deviation 1
Engine policy with no performance threshold: every metric is descriptive and the criterion stays inconclusive (no_threshold), as today
Engine multiclass policy with only an accuracy minimum: the derived criterion adds the macro-recall chance baseline 1/k, on which a constant majority-class predictor sits, so it cannot pass
Engine binary policy with a balanced-accuracy minimum below chance: the baseline is max(0.5, 0.40), on which a constant negative predictor sits, so it cannot pass
Engine regression policy with an R2 minimum and a mean predictor (R2 = 0): MAE and RMSE pass, but R2, which 1.0.0 cannot decide, blocks the pass
Legacy hosted multiclass profile: the derived criterion adds the macro-recall chance baseline 1/3 between accuracy and macro F1, and the GC-34 model passes all three

GC-47's policy and a predictor that rarely says positive: one lucky positive (TP 1 of 100) puts the balanced-accuracy interval above 0.5, but the exact chance gate does not reject, so the criterion is inconclusive

GC-46's policy and a predictor that rarely predicts two of three classes: one correct 'high' puts the macro-recall interval above 1/3, but the exact chance gate (Bonferroni over the classes) does not reject, so the criterion is inconclusive
